name: Shimoyakebe large-seeded soybean
description: Large soybean seeds at Shimoyakebe are interpreted as evidence consistent with human selection.

impact.note: Large seeds at one site only consistent with selection; a modest gain if real, and no descent to later soybean farming is shown.

date.label: Approximately 5,000 cal BP (3050 BCE)
date.basis: Lee and colleagues’ approximate age of the Mid-Jomon find, based on directly dated charred Glycine seed PLD-9088 and the midden context.

events.statement: Large soybean seeds at Shimoyakebe are interpreted as evidence consistent with human selection.

evidence.supports: The researchers compare soybean seed sizes and identify large Middle Jomon specimens at Shimoyakebe around 5,000 calibrated years before 1950, interpreting enlargement as evidence consistent with selection. Size is an imperfect proxy for domestication, and the finding does not establish a single point of origin.

evidence.locator: Table 1, sample SY 37 (PLD-9088); English summary p. 26
evidence.supports: Original report of the directly dated charred Glycine seed from the Middle Jomon walnut midden. It documents the same dated specimen cited by Lee and colleagues.

events.caveats: The approximate date summarizes a Middle Jomon assemblage; the study reports an AMS date directly on a charred soybean and notes agreement with other material. Seed size alone cannot prove domestication, cultivation or unique origin; selection is the authors’ inference.

earliest_record.rationale: Date of this particular documented case, not a claim of global priority.
